portfolio.codebook_interaction: The usage-balancing component adjusts codewords through their soft-assignment probabilities, while the centroid barrier repels codewords from an overly tight centroid geometry. The directed KL component penalizes source and target assignment distributions that become indistinguishable. These terms do not minimize the distance between a transition's two codewords; the KL term instead favors different endpoint distributions. A zero barrier gradient can occur when the separation threshold is already met.
portfolio.falsifier: Reject if the cold run's exported level-0 Gini exceeds the control's 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.
portfolio.risk: Uniform soft usage and a centroid-spread barrier may preserve code usage without preserving useful item distinctions; the directed KL can also over-separate common transitions. The soft objective may not translate into hard assignment changes, and the frozen run could therefore fail to improve Stage-3 retrieval despite healthy soft statistics.

portfolio.codebook_interaction: The transport-alignment term updates the source- and target-weighted codebook vectors to represent the directed residual. The overlap penalty discourages shared endpoint assignments, and the source-marginal concentration penalty discourages excessive usage imbalance. The alignment term does not minimize the distance between the two endpoint codewords; the overlap penalty actively discourages assignment convergence.
